exercises.title: Cedar Court: GPR to DSCR
exercises.intro: Build Cedar Court's underwritten cash flow one line at a time, from GPR to DSCR. Each line is checked before the next opens.

buildup.context: Cedar Court (RD-MF-01): 50 units at $1,300 market rent. Rent-roll collections annualized $702,000; trailing 3 months annualized $708,000; other income (T-12) $18,000. Expenses: T-12 $298,000; appraiser $310,000, including 4% management. Replacement reserves $15,000 a year. Bridge test debt service is $4,340,000 × 8.25% = $358,050.00.

lines.label: Underwritten vacancy rate (MF-GEN-05)
lines.hint: Collections are the lesser of $702,000 and $708,000. Vacancy rate = 1 − $702,000 ÷ $780,000. It is above the 5% floor.

lines.label: Underwritten operating expenses (MF-GEN-06)
lines.hint: Take the greater of the T-12 and the appraiser's estimate. Management at 4% of EGI clears the 3% floor.

lines.label: DSCR on NOI (F-CORE-11)
lines.hint: $410,000 ÷ $358,050. Compare at full precision: it is 1.1451.

exercises.title: Break-even occupancy
exercises.intro: Find Cedar Court's break-even occupancy and its cushion. Then change expenses, debt service or GPR to see how fast the cushion moves.

calculator.task: Cedar Court: OpEx $310,000, test ADS $358,050 and GPR $780,000. What is break-even occupancy (F-CORE-12)? Then subtract it from 90.0% economic occupancy to get the cushion.

exercises.title: Spot the error: the broker's NOI
exercises.intro: A broker's package shows a much higher NOI than your underwriting. Find what is wrong with it, and say which figure we lend on.

scenario.case: The broker's one-page summary for Cedar Court shows NOI of $575,000. It divides that by the $358,050 bridge test debt service and reports DSCR of 1.61x. Your underwriting shows NOI of $410,000 and DSCR of 1.15x.
scenario.prompt: What is wrong with the broker's $575,000? Name where the gap comes from, which NOI we size the day-one loan on, and where the $575,000 does belong.
scenario.model_answer: The $575,000 is a pro forma. It is stabilized NOI after the $800,000 renovation: stabilized NCF $560,000 plus $15,000 reserves. The renovation has not happened, so the $165,000 gap is not yet earned. We size the day-one loan on in-place NOI of $410,000 (F-CORE-10). That uses the lesser of rent roll and trailing 3 months for income (MF-GEN-05). It also uses the greater of T-12 and appraiser for expenses (MF-GEN-06). DSCR on that NOI is $410,000 ÷ $358,050 = 1.15x (F-CORE-11), not 1.61x. The stabilized figures belong only in the exit test: $560,000 NCF (MF-BR-08, F-MF-20). At a 7.00% loan constant, the $165,000 gap is worth about $2.4 million of loan.
rubric: Says the $575,000 is stabilized, pro forma NOI after the renovation, not in-place NOI
Uses in-place NOI of $410,000 for day-one sizing
Names the income and expense rules: lesser of rent roll and T-3 (MF-GEN-05); greater of T-12 and appraiser (MF-GEN-06)
Places the stabilized figure in the exit test only: $560,000 NCF = $575,000 − $15,000 reserves (MF-BR-08)
